key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky imagery with RMSE close to a model trained on the complete dataset.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly irradiance sensors for photovoltaic performance optimisation and solar energy forecasting.
method: Add calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings.
Predict synthetic global horizontal irradiance first, then use it to refine diffuse irradiance estimates.
Process raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye images in parallel using unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation.
evidence_signal: At Chilbolton Observatory, single-month training and temporally disjoint full-year testing yielded RMSE within 2–3 W/m² for the sequential framework and 1–6 W/m² for the dual-parallel framework of a full-dataset ViT baseline.
watch_item: Validation at one temperate-climate site leaves generalisation to other climates and camera setups unproven.
paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
